[s0l0!-header][h1]Pointers[/h1][/s0l0!-header]

Every variable is a [b]memory [/b]location, which has its [b]address [/b]defined. 
That address can be accessed using the [b]ampersand (&)[/b] operator (also called the address-of operator), which denotes an[b] address in memory[/b].

[s0l0!-header][b]For example:[/b][/s0l0!-header][code format="cpp" codeId="222"]int score = 5;
cout << [b]&[/b]score << endl;
[/code]
[note]This outputs the [b]memory address[/b], which stores the variable [b]score[/b].[/note]

resolved.title: 指针
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Pointers[/h1][/s0l0!-header]

A [b]pointer [/b]is a variable, with the address of another variable as its value.
In C++, pointers help make certain tasks easier to perform. Other tasks, such as dynamic memory allocation, cannot be performed without using pointers.

All pointers share the same data type - a long [b]hexadecimal [/b]number that represents a memory address.
[note]The only difference between pointers of different data types is the data type of the variable that the pointer points to.[/note]
resolved.description_en:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Pointers[/h1][/s0l0!-header]

content.text:
一个**指针**是一个变量，以另一个变量的地址作为其值。

在C++中，指针有助于使某些任务更容易执行。如动态内存分配，如果不使用指针就无法执行。

所有指针的值的实际数据类型，不管是整型、浮点型、字符型，还是其他的数据类型，都是一样的：十六进制数表示的内存地址。
content.text_html:
A **pointer **is a variable, with the address of another variable as its value. In C++, pointers help make certain tasks easier to perform. Other tasks, such as dynamic memory allocation, cannot be performed without using pointers.

All pointers share the same data type - a long **hexadecimal **number that represents a memory address.

一个指针是一个变量，以另一个变量的地址作为其值。 在C++中，指针有助于使某些任务更容易执行。其他任务，如动态内存分配，如果不使用指针就无法执行。

所有的指针都有相同的数据类型--一个长的十六进制的数字，代表一个内存地址。

content.text: 不同数据类型的指针之间的唯一区别：指针所指向的变量的数据类型。
content.text_html:
The only difference between pointers of different data types is the data type of the variable that the pointer points to.

不同数据类型的指针之间的唯一区别是指针所指向的变量的数据类型。

resolved.title: 指针
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Pointers[/h1][/s0l0!-header]

A [b]pointer [/b]is a variable, and like any other variable, it must be declared before you can work with it. 
The [b]asterisk [/b]sign is used to declare a pointer (the same asterisk that you use for multiplication), however, in this statement the asterisk is being used to designate a variable as a pointer. 
Following are valid pointer declarations: [code format="cpp" ]int *ip;  // pointer to an integer
double *dp;   // pointer to a double
float *fp;  // pointer to a float
char *ch;  // pointer to a character[/code]
Just like with variables, we give the pointers a name and define the type, to which the pointer points to.
[note]The asterisk sign can be placed next to the data type, or the variable name, or in the middle.[/note]
